items.text: COMMITTEE DISCHARGED AND COMMITTED TO RULES
ORDERED TO THIRD READING RULES CAL.144

items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the public health law, in relation to requiring the commissioner of health to post information detailing how parents or guardians of infants or children can subscribe to the US Consumer Safety Product Commission's (CSPC) e-mail subscription lists to receive free product recall and safety news by e-mail from the CSPC and requiring the inclusion of such information in maternity information leaflets
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S7441

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the public health law, in relation to requiring the
commissioner of health to post information detailing how parents or
guardians of infants or children can subscribe to the US Consumer
Safety Product Commission's (CSPC) e-mail subscription lists to
receive free product recall and safety news by e-mail from the CSPC
and requiring the inclusion of such information in maternity
information leaflets


 PURPOSE :
To prevent children's injuries and/or deaths by making parents and
guardians aware of objects harmful to a child's health by providing
information on how to sign up for e-mail alerts from the Consumer
Product Safety Commission upon the reception of maternity information
leaflets. The parents are not only given information on how to sign up
for the alerts, but are also made aware that the CPSC exists, and does
so to protect the well-being of families and individuals.

 JUSTIFICATION :
In 2009, the Consumer Product Safety Commission released a report
stating that 19 toy-related deaths and 235,300 toy-related injuries
occurred in 2008. By giving parents information on how to sign up for
e-mail alerts, and allowing them to know that such e-mail alerts
exist, these injuries and deaths could easily be prevented.

If a parent happens to skip over a news article or report regarding a
toy recall, the lives of their children could be endangered. Although
there is no perfect method or dependable source for notifying parents
about dangerous products that may be in their households, this bill
would help to ensure the safety of young children in New York State.

In 2009, this Legislature passed a bill which also requires the same
facilities to distribute, in the same maternity leaflet, information
on basic breastfeeding related rights; and which also requires posting
of the list of rights on the health department's website.  This bill
has the same intent, but also, literally, saves lives and protects our
children from serious injury.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect on the first of May next succeeding The
date on which it shall have become a law; provided, however, that
effective immediately, the addition, amendment and/or repeal of any
rule or regulation necessary for the implementation of this act on its
effective date are authorized and directed to be made and completed by
the commissioner of health on or before such effective date.

A.actClause: AN ACT to amend the public health law, in relation to requiring hospitals and birth centers to prepare and distribute an informational leaflet containing information detailing how parents or guardians of infants and children can subscribe to the United States consumer product safety commission's e-mail subscription lists to receive consumer product recall and safety news
A.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S7441A

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the public health law, in relation to requiring
hospitals and birth centers to prepare and distribute an informational
leaflet containing information detailing how parents or guardians of
infants and children can subscribe to the United States consumer
product safety commission's e-mail subscription lists to receive
consumer product recall and safety news


 PURPOSE :
To prevent children's injuries and/or deaths by making parents and
guardians aware of products that may be harmful to a child's health by
providing information on how to sign up for e-mail alerts from the
United States Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC). The parents
are not only given information on how to sign up for the alerts, but
are also made aware that the CPSC exists, and does so to protect the
wellbeing of families and individuals.

This bill would require hospital and birth centers to distribute an

Protection Board.

 JUSTIFICATION :
In 2009, the Consumer Product Safety Commission released a report
stating that 19 toy-related deaths and 235,300 toy-related injuries
occurred in 2008. By giving parents information on how to sign up for
e-mail alerts, and allowing them to know that such e-mail alerts
exist, these injuries and deaths could easily be prevented.

If a parent happens to skip over a news article or report regarding a
toy recall, the lives of their children could be endangered. Although
there is no perfect method or dependable source for notifying parents
about dangerous products that may be in their households, this bill
would help to ensure the safety of young children in New York State.

In 2009, this Legislature passed a bill that also requires the same
facilities to distribute information on basic breast feeding related
rights; and which requires posting of the list of rights on the health
department's website. This bill has the same intent, but also,
literally saves lives and protects our children from serious injury.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
None.

This act shall take effect on the first of May next succeeding The
date on which it shall have become a law; provided, however, that
effective immediately, the addition, amendment and/or repeal of any
rule or regulation necessary for the implementation of this act on its
effective date are authorized and directed to be made and completed by

lation necessary for the implementation of this act on its effective

sioner of health on or before such effective date.
